 Prayer : Writ Petition filed under Article 226 of Constitution of India   for the issuance of a Writ of Declaration, declaring that the Award No.1  dated 06.11.1975, passed by the second respondent herein as lapsed under  Section 24 of Right to fair Compensation and Transparency in Land  Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Re-settlement Act 2013 in so far as Old   (Cadastre) No.1747 1/4, 1747 2/4, 1747 3/4, 1748 2/4, 1748 3/4, Re.Surve  271/4b, Thattanchavady Revenue Village, Puducherry for the reason of not  taking possession which was expressly recorded in award and consequently  forbear the respondents from disturbing petitioner's possession based on  land acquisition proceedings vide award No.17/75 dated 06.11.1975.
For Petitioner : Mr.Prakash Adiyapadam  for Mr.V.Moorthi  For Respondents : Mr.V.Vasanthakumar
Additional
Government
Plea  ORDER

This writ petition has been filed for declaration declaring the Award 17/75 dated 06.11.1975 on the file of the second respondent as lapsed under Section 24 of Right to fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Re-settlement Act 2013 (herein after called as the New Act) in so far as Old S.No. (Cadastre) No.1747 1/4, 1747 2/4, 1747 3/4, 1748 2/4, 1748 3/4,
Re.Survey No.271/4b, Thattanchavady Revenue Village, Puducherry.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Heard the learned counsel on either side and perused the materials available on record.

3. The land comprised in Old S.No. (Cadastre) No.1747 1/4, 1747 2/4, 1747 3/4, 1748 2/4, 1748 3/4,
Re.Survey No.271/4b, Thattanchavady Revenue Village, Puducherry originally owned by one Sellapa W/o Arumugan Muthu @ Subburayan and D/o Murugan @ Mottai.
It was acquired for the purpose of widening the Tindivanam High Road by National Highway Authority of India.

After acquisition,
the land ad-measuring 00.14.40 HA is in possession and enjoyment of the petitioner.

That apart,
though the Award was passed in respect of the subject property, no compensation amount was paid to the petitioner.

Thereafter, the third respondent issued a show cause notice under the Public Premises Eviction of Unauthorized Occupants Act, 1971, thereby calling upon the petitioner to vacate the subject property, on the ground that the lands were acquired by the second respondent by the Award No.17/75 dated 06.11.1975.

entities.text: Public Premises Eviction of Unauthorized Occupants Act, 1971
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: It was challenged before this Court in W.P.No.21253 of 2018 and the same was allowed and remanded back to conduct fresh enquiry and pass orders.

Therefore,
the petitioner sought for declaration of the entire Award proceeding as lapsed under Section 24(2)
of the New Act.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis

A perusal of the counter and also on the submissions made by the learned Additional Government Pleader (Pondy) revealed that the lands comprised in Survey Nos.1747 to 1754 to an extent of Sadasivam Adiparamasvary vs Union Of India on 7 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76945934/
2 0.95.45 hectares situated in Oulgaret commune (Thattanchavady Village) were acquired by the Government for the provision of house sites to Harijans.

entities.text: Sadasivam Adiparamasvary vs Union Of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thereafter, the Award was passed on 06.11.1975 in Award No.17/75.
The possession of the entire land was taken over and handed over to the Harijan Welfare Inspector, Department for the welfare of Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribes, Pondicherry.
Insofar as the award compensation is concerned, a sum of Rs.3449.89 under Form D, the amount has been deposited in the Civil Court in LAOP.No.43 of 1976.
Therefore, the petitioner had failed to satisfy the twin conditions as required under Section 24(2) of the New Act.
5. In view of the above, the writ petition is devoid of merits and is liable to be dismissed.
Accordingly, this writ petition stands dismissed.
Consequently, connected Miscellaneous petitions are closed.
No costs.
